ai.title: Fix missing propose prefix in editor-implementor tool names
ai.summary: Corrects `cb_tool_name` values in the `editor-implementor` prompt from `str_replace` and `write_file` to `propose_str_replace` and `propose_write_file`. This aligns the prompt instructions with the actual tool definitions, ensuring the agent uses the correct namespaced tools for proposing edits. The fix applies to the best-of-n editor agent implementation.

eli5.text: The automated editor agent is now calling its file-editing helpers by the correct, namespaced names instead of generic ones, so it consistently uses the proposal variants of the tools rather than plain replacements. This corrects a mismatch between the instructions the agent was given and the actual tools available to it, preventing it from attempting to invoke tools that aren't properly scoped to proposing changes. If you watched the agent working today, you wouldn't notice this directly, but it ensures the agent's edit operations are properly routed through the correct proposing workflow rather than generic ones.

ai.title: /review command added to CLI with GPT-5 Agent integration
ai.summary: New /review slash command added to CLI. Command registry handler in command-registry.ts checks for args: if present, sends '@GPT-5 Agent Please review: <args>' directly; if absent, returns openReviewScreen flag. ReviewScreen component in review-screen.tsx provides selection UI for 'Uncommitted changes', 'This branch vs main', and 'Custom...' modes. State managed via zustand store in review-store.ts. Chat component in chat.tsx disables keyboard handlers when reviewMode active and wires handleReviewOptionSelect to submit prompt with current agentMode. Slash commands list updated in slash-commands.ts.

eli5.text: You can now get help reviewing your code by typing a new command directly into the chat. When you type the review command with specific text, the assistant immediately examines those changes without any extra steps; if you type it without text, a simple on-screen menu appears letting you choose to examine your recent changes, this branch compared to the main version, or enter a custom review request. The feature is live today and appears in the list of available commands whenever you open the chat.

ai.title: Add /theme:toggle command to CLI
ai.summary: New /theme:toggle slash command flips between light and dark themes. Handler reads current theme from useThemeStore, sets the opposite name, and injects a system confirmation message. Registered in command-registry.ts and exposed in slash-commands.ts for autocomplete.

eli5.text: You can now press /theme:toggle at the command line to instantly flip your screen between the light and dark color scheme, and a brief message will confirm which one is now active. Behind the scenes, the program reads your current theme choice from its shared settings, switches it to the opposite option, updates those settings so the new look sticks, and then clears the command line so you can keep working. The command is also now visible when you start typing a slash, so it shows up in the autocompletion list alongside the other built-in commands. This is live today for anyone running the CLI.

ai.summary: SuggestionMenu `maxVisible` in `chat-input-bar.tsx` now derives from `terminalHeight > 35 ? 15 : 10` instead of hardcoded 10. Applies to both `/` slash and `@` mention menus. Scope limited to CLI component; no model or API change.

eli5.text: When you open the command or mention menu in the CLI on a large terminal, the list now shows up to 15 options at once instead of 10. This applies to both the slash commands menu and the mention menu, making it easier to browse more suggestions without scrolling. The menu automatically switches between 10 and 15 items based on whether your terminal has more than 35 lines of height.

These entries were commented out in the command list file, removing them from the picker without deleting anything permanently. The change affects anyone using the CLI slash commands today and live.

ai.title: 1.0.607 adds /review, /theme:toggle, and PromptResult abort handling
ai.summary: Release 1.0.607 ships the new /review slash command, which sends '@GPT-5 Agent Please review: <args>' when args are provided or opens a ReviewScreen with modes for uncommitted changes, branch vs main, and custom input. The /theme:toggle command flips between light and dark themes via useThemeStore and injects a system confirmation. Under the hood, common, agent-runtime, and SDK LLM paths now use the PromptResult union type and AbortError so user aborts propagate immediately instead of triggering fallback model calls, and the CLI fingerprints hardware via node-machine-id and systeminformation for deterministic auth IDs.
ai.evidence: Diff in cli/release/package.json bumps version from 1.0.606 to 1.0.607; release updates include new /review slash command (command-registry.ts handler + ReviewScreen + review-store.ts), /theme:toggle (useThemeStore), PromptResult/AbortError refactor across common/src/util/error.ts and sdk/src/impl/llm.ts, and hardware fingerprinting via use-fingerprint hook.

eli5.text: This release adds a built-in code review tool to the CLI and makes it easier to flip between light and dark themes on the fly. You can now run a new /review command that lets you ask GPT-5 Agent to scan uncommitted changes, compare your branch against main, or review custom code you specify, all from a simple selection screen. A new /theme:toggle command lets you switch color schemes instantly without restarting. Aborting long-running requests now behaves more cleanly, so canceling an in-progress task stops immediately instead of burning time switching to backup models. The terminal suggestion menus stretch taller on large screens, and a couple of niche agent actions were quietly removed from the command list.

ai.title: Remove browser auto-open from CLI plain login
ai.summary: Plain login in cli/src/login/plain-login.ts no longer attempts to open a browser via the 'open' package. It now displays the login URL and instructs the user to open it manually. This simplifies the flow and removes dependency on local browser availability.

eli5.text: When you sign in from the command line, the tool will no longer try to launch your web browser automatically. Instead it prints the login address and tells you to open it yourself in a browser tab. You'll see the same login URL as before, but the line that used to say "Browser opened" now says "Please open the URL above manually to complete login." This is live today for anyone using the plain login flow on a server or machine where no browser is guaranteed to be available.

ai.title: CLI ships 1.0.608 with /review GPT-5 Agent, /theme:toggle, and plain
ai.summary: Version 1.0.608 rolls up the same-day CLI changes into the release package at cli/release/package.json. This release includes the new /review slash command that either sends '@GPT-5 Agent Please review: <args>' when args are present or opens a ReviewScreen UI for selecting 'Uncommitted changes', 'This branch vs main', or 'Custom...' review modes. It also adds /theme:toggle to flip between light and dark themes via useThemeStore, and updates plain login in cli/src/login/plain-login.ts to display the login URL directly instead of attempting to auto-open a browser with the 'open' package.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field changed from "1.0.607" to "1.0.608"; surrounding same-day work included /review and /theme:toggle slash commands (commit 61912309) and the removal of browser auto-open from plain login (commit 7970c2de).

eli5.text: This update makes it easier to start a secure login with Freebuff by showing you a web address you can open yourself, instead of trying to launch a browser automatically which sometimes failed. You get a smoother and more reliable login experience that works even if your computer doesn't have a default web browser set up properly, and you no longer need extra software installed just to sign in.

ai.title: Suppress flaky validate-agents network errors
ai.summary: CLI hook use-send-message.ts now returns an empty error array when validation fails with no specific errors, suppressing the generic network error message. This mitigates noise from flaky validate endpoint responses. Changes also harden ValidationErrorPopover.tsx against undefined error IDs by defaulting to empty strings and using index-based keys, and update sdk validate-agents.ts to default error.filePath to 'unknown' if missing.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to double-check your agents before sending a message and that check hits a temporary server hiccup, you will now simply see your message go through without a noisy "network error" popup. The system used to show a generic error notice whenever the validation step returned no specific problems; now it quietly treats that blank result as a pass and only surfaces real, specific validation issues if any appear. Behind the scenes, the error list display also guards against missing identifiers so it won't break if an agent ID comes back empty, and the underlying validation tool now labels a missing file path as 'unknown' instead of leaving it blank.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.609 release with validate-agents noise suppression
ai.summary: Bumped the Freebuff CLI package version to 1.0.609 in cli/release/package.json. Ships the companion change that suppresses flaky generic network errors when the validate-agents endpoint returns responses without specific errors, while hardening the validation error popover and defaulting sdk validate-agents filePath to ‘unknown’ when missing. This release rolls up the preceding same-day CLI work around slash-command behavior and terminal rendering alongside the validation noise fix.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI version 1.0.609 quiets down a noisy error alert that would pop up during agent validation, making your terminal cleaner and less distracting. The update fixes a bug where a generic network error message would appear even when there was no real error to show, and it makes the software more stable when validation checks return incomplete or unexpected information. Upgrading gives you a smoother, quieter command-line experience with fewer false alarms interrupting your workflow.

ai.title: Remove debug log from message queue
ai.summary: Removed a `logger.debug` call in `use-message-queue.ts` that logged when the queue was blocked. This reduces console noise during CLI operation. The change is internal to the CLI's message processing logic.

eli5.text: The CLI stopped printing a debug message that previously appeared in the console when the assistant's message queue was temporarily blocked from sending responses. You may have seen technical diagnostic text about the queue being blocked in your terminal before; that line of text will no longer appear. This is purely a cosmetic change that reduces console noise during normal CLI operation, with no impact on functionality.

ai.title: Gravity API error handling: parse JSON only after response.ok check
ai.summary: `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts` now checks `response.ok` before parsing JSON to prevent unhandled exceptions when Gravity API returns HTML error pages. Error responses are logged with raw text if content-type is not `application/json`. Added empty array guard: `ads.length === 0` returns `{ ad: null }` with debug log. Scope: server-side ads API only.

eli5.text: If you visit a page that asks for a sponsored post and the ad service behind it returns an error instead of an ad, the page now stays calm instead of crashing. It checks whether the service said ‘all good’ before trying to read the response, so broken or non-ad replies (like a plain text or HTML error) are logged quietly and you simply see no ad rather than an error screen. This only affects the server-side tool that picks which promoted post to show, so nothing on your end changes except fewer surprise breakages.

ai.title: Referral bonuses shift to one-time 500 credits
ai.summary: Referral bonuses converted from monthly recurring to one-time grants, increasing amount from 250 to 500 credits. New `referral` grants never expire, while legacy recurring referrals marked with `is_legacy=true` migrate to `referral_legacy` type with priority 30. Changes affect `common/src/constants/limits.ts`, `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`, and new migration `0039_quiet_franklin_storm.sql`.

eli5.text: When you refer a friend now, you get a single 500-credit bonus instead of a monthly trickle, and those new one-time bonuses never expire. Anyone who signed up for referral credits under the old program is shifted to the legacy track, which still pays out monthly but is drawn down before other credits. The change is live today as part of this week's release, and you can tell it worked by checking your referral history: old entries now show a one-time 500 credit grant instead of recurring monthly amounts.

ai.title: Split referrallegacy migration for PostgreSQL enum
ai.summary: Referral legacy backfill logic moved from 0039_quiet_franklin_storm.sql to new 0040_referral_legacy_backfill.sql. PostgreSQL forbids ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE and subsequent DML in same transaction; splitting resolves this. 0039 now sets is_legacy default to true directly, removing explicit UPDATE. Affects packages/internal/src/db/migrations.

eli5.text: The system that tracks referral rewards had to reorganize how it stores old vs. new referral data to keep the database healthy. The assistant can now correctly mark existing referrals as "legacy" without running into a database restriction that previously stopped the process. Nothing visible changes for you yet since this was just moving around behind the scenes how the data gets labeled and updated.

ai.title: packages/internal db:migrate switches drizzle-kit push to migrate
ai.summary: packages/internal/package.json db:migrate script calls drizzle-kit migrate instead of drizzle-kit push. Avoids push's direct schema sync for safer production deployments. Scoped to packages/internal. db:start still chains docker compose up, db:generate, then db:migrate.

eli5.text: When the internal team sets up or updates the database for this package, the command now builds a careful step-by-step record of the changes instead of immediately rewriting the database structure to match the code. This makes the database updates safer to run in production, where directly changing the live structure can cause problems. If you ran the setup steps, you would not notice anything different on screen, but the underlying process that modifies the database is now more cautious and reliable.

ai.title: Move referral backfill out of Drizzle migration
ai.summary: Referral legacy backfill removed from `0040_referral_legacy_backfill.sql` and moved to manual `scripts/backfill-referral-legacy.sql`. Drizzle journal updated to drop migration 40. PostgreSQL requires new enum values to be committed before use in subsequent statements, causing transaction failures in automated migrations. Operators must run the script via `psql` after deploying migration 0039.

eli5.text: The system that automatically updates your account's old referral credit records has been changed so it no longer runs automatically during software updates. Instead, the database team now runs it manually as a separate step right after the update is deployed. This was done because the automated system was failing due to a technical limitation in how the database handles new kinds of referral types. You won't notice anything different in your account unless you're one of the few people with old referral credits that haven't been converted yet, in which case your account will get updated manually in the next maintenance window.

ai.title: fix(db): Remove trailing comma in migration journal JSON
ai.summary: Removed trailing comma from `packages/internal/src/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json`. Prevents JSON parse errors in strict parsers. Affects internal DB migration metadata.

eli5.text: When you create a new database, the system reads a list that records every change made to its structure. That list had a stray comma at the end of one entry, which strict reading rules treat as a syntax error, similar to a misspelled word tripping up a spell-checker. Fixing that comma ensures the list is read correctly when setting up the database, but otherwise you will not notice any difference in how things work.
